bills.title: Conversational AI Disclosures for Minors
bills.summary: Requires operators of conversational AI services to provide disclosures for minor users and prohibit them from generating statements to minor account holders that simulate emotional dependence and romantic innuendos, among other requirements.

bills.title: Prohibition on Companion Chatbot Toys
bills.summary: Would prohibit the manufacture, sale, exchange, or possession with intent to sell any toy that contains a companion chatbot.

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Law Expansion
bills.summary: Would expand last year's companion chatbot law (SB 243), revising the standard triggering operator obligations from 'knows a user is a minor' to an 'actual knowledge' standard, and removing 'reasonable measures' language to simply require operators to 'prevent' exchanges of sexually explicit content. Passed Senate Judiciary Committee 13-Y 0-N on 1/13.
bills.status_detail: Passed Senate Judiciary Committee 13-Y 0-N on January 13, 2026

bills.title: Data Center Transparency Act
bills.summary: The 'Data Center Transparency Act' would require data centers to disclose specified information, including energy management plans and greenhouse gas emissions.

bills.title: Chatbot Disclosure Requirements
bills.summary: Introduced by the Committee on Technology, this bill would set disclosure requirements for chatbots (not minor specific). Requirements include prohibiting chatbots from encouraging violence or self harm, setting disclosure requirements every 30 minutes, and prohibiting representation as a medical, legal, financial, or psychological services professional.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by the Committee on Technology

bills.title: Saving Human Connection Act
bills.summary: The 'Saving Human Connection Act' would prohibit chatbots with human-like features from being made available to minors and require reasonable age verification systems. Among other requirements, the bill would prohibit covered platforms from processing data in ways that conflict with a user's best interests.

bills.title: Protecting Consumers and Jobs from Predatory Pricing Act
bills.summary: The 'Protecting Consumers and Jobs from Predatory Pricing Act' would require disclosures for any business that engages in personalized algorithmic pricing using individualized consumer data. Would also prohibit businesses from using electronic shelving labels to display personalized algorithmic pricing. Includes a private right of action.

bills.title: Prohibition on Advertising AI as Mental Health Professional
bills.summary: Would prohibit advertising AI as a mental health professional.

bills.title: Data Center Clean Energy Requirements
bills.summary: Requires energy usage plans for data centers that mandate all electricity be sourced from new clean energy sources.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Sen. Smith (D) and Sen. McKeon (D)

bills.title: AI Safety Testing and Reporting Requirements
bills.summary: Requires AI companies to conduct safety tests and to send the results to the state Office of Information Technology.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Sen. Singleton (D) and Sen. McKnight (D)

bills.title: GenAI Whistleblower Protection Resolution
bills.summary: Urges GenAI companies to make voluntary commitments regarding employee whistleblower protections.

bills.title: AI Disclosure at Point of Customer Interaction
bills.summary: Would require any person to disclose the use of AI to influence customer interaction, including automated customer support and personalized ad targeting. The disclosure would be required at the point of interaction with the consumer where the customer first encounters AI.

bills.title: Automated Employment Decision Tool Disclosure for Government
bills.summary: Would require disclosure of any automated employment decision making tools (AEDMTs) used by cities, counties, schools, and other government entities. The bill would also state that the use of AI systems shall not result in the discharge, displacement, or reduction in wages of employees.

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Age Verification Requirements
bills.summary: Modeled on the federal CHAT Act, would require age verification for individuals seeking access to a companion chatbot. The bill would also require disclosures every 30 minutes of use and prohibit representations as a licensed professional.

bills.title: Prohibition on Human-Like Chatbots for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from being made available to minors if they have human-like features and would require the implementation of reasonable age-verification systems.

bills.title: AI Limitations for Mental Health Practitioners
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill that limits the use of AI by mental health practitioners.

bills.title: Prohibition on AI Advertising as Mental Health Professional
bills.summary: Would prohibit the development or deployment of an AI system that advertises that it is able to act as a qualified mental health professional.

bills.title: AI Therapy Prohibition
bills.summary: Modeled on Illinois HB 1806, would prohibit persons from providing AI therapy unless provided by a licensed professional. Would also prohibit licensed professionals from using AI in administrative or supplementary support functions unless they maintain full responsibility for all interactions.

bills.title: AI Therapy Prohibition (Senate)
bills.summary: Modeled on Illinois HB 1806, would prohibit persons from providing AI therapy unless provided by a licensed professional. Would also prohibit licensed professionals from using AI in administrative or supplementary support functions unless they maintain full responsibility for all interactions.

bills.title: Prohibition on Human-Like Chatbots for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from being made available to minors if they have human-like features and would require the implementation of reasonable age-verification systems.

bills.title: Prohibition on Chatbots Providing Licensed Professional Advice
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from providing any substantive information or advice that could constitute the practice of a variety of licensed professions, including medicine, social work, engineering, dentistry, and more.

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Safety and Privacy Requirements
bills.summary: Modeled in part on California's AB 1018. Would prohibit making companion chatbots available to minors unless they are incapable of certain harmful behaviors, such as encouraging disordered eating or self-isolation. Would also require disclosures every 30 minutes and impose data privacy restrictions including prohibiting training companion chatbots on minors' inputs without written parental consent.

bills.title: AI Limitations for Mental Health Practitioners
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill that limits the use of AI by mental health practitioners.

bills.title: AI Limitations for Mental Health Practitioners (Senate)
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill that limits the use of AI by mental health practitioners.

bills.title: AI Fraud and Abuse Alert System
bills.summary: Would establish a program under the Department of Law to address AI fraud and abuse, including establishing a statewide AI fraud and abuse alert system.

bills.title: Base AI Model Terms of Service Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require AI model developers of base AI models to disclose the terms of service governing their model, including the model and developer's name.

bills.title: AI System Independent Verification Organization Framework
bills.summary: Would create a framework for any person or entity seeking to act as an independent verification organization (IVO) to audit AI systems for prevention of personal injury and property damage.

bills.title: Automated Decision System Disclosures and Bias Assessments
bills.summary: Would require disclosures when ADS is used to make a decision related to employment, education, or access to public accommodations and would require annual assessments by deployers for bias and discriminatory impact, including evaluation of training data and outputs.

bills.title: Centralized AI Coordination Program in AG Office
bills.summary: Would establish a centralized program within the AG's office to coordinate Virginia's response to AI, algorithmic systems, biometric systems, and ADMTs. Among other obligations, the AG would be required to maintain a public process to receive complaints regarding these technologies.

bills.title: VCDPA AI System Obligations and Social Media Protections for Minors
bills.summary: Would require controllers and processors of AI systems to exercise reasonable care to protect consumers from known or foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination and set other obligations for controllers, such as obtaining consent from consumers before using their data. Would also require that controllers register with the Commonwealth including submitting the privacy policy for the AI system. Amends VCDPA to increase social media protections for minors.

bills.title: Fair Pricing and Transparency Act
bills.summary: The 'Fair Pricing and Transparency Act' would prohibit the use of surveillance-based price discrimination to modify goods prices for consumers, including the use of surge pricing to modify the price of goods regardless of frequency or duration.

bills.title: High-Risk AI System Disclosure and Algorithmic Discrimination Protections
bills.summary: A VA HB 2094-style bill that would set disclosure requirements for developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems and set protections against reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Would establish an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.
bills.status_detail: Already passed the House and on track to pass the Senate

bills.title: Parents Over Platforms Act Age Signals Framework
bills.summary: Mirrors the Parents Over Platforms Act, requiring application distribution providers to ask account holders to declare their age and provide developers of covered applications the ability to call an age signal. Would also require additional age assurance obligations for developers.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Would establish an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Sen. Calatayud (R) on January 9, 2026

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Framework with Social Media Safety
bills.summary: An App Store Accountability Act framework aligning with models enacted in Utah, Louisiana, and Texas in 2025. Would provide a private right of action for harmed minors and their parents. Also contains a section with safety-related protections for social media platforms.

bills.title: GDPR-Style Comprehensive Consumer Privacy Bill
bills.summary: A GDPR-style comprehensive consumer privacy bill with a lawful basis requirement, introduced alongside New Jersey's existing comprehensive privacy law.
bills.status_detail: Introduced in the new legislative session

bills.title: Deidentification Requirement Prior to Personal Data Sale
bills.summary: A proposed amendment to New Jersey's existing comprehensive privacy law that would require controllers to deidentify personal data prior to selling it.
bills.status_detail: Introduced in the new legislative session

bills.title: Age-Appropriate Design Code (AADC)
bills.summary: A framework inspired by the Senate version of KOSA, establishing age-appropriate design code requirements. The House voted unanimously to approve and return an amended version to the Senate with changes including adjustments to proposed definitions, Nebraska AADC-style requirements for tools a covered online service must provide, and amendments to the effective date to take effect upon the Governor's approval.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; in ratification process before Governor McMaster

bills.title: GLBA Data-Level Exemption for Reproductive Health Information
bills.summary: Would add a GLBA data-level exemption to the reproductive or sexual health information amendment to Virginia's consumer protection act passed last year.

bills.title: VCDPA Verifiable Parental Consent Requirement for Minors
bills.summary: Would require controllers or processors to obtain verifiable parental consent for minors under the age of 18 prior to registering for the product or service or prior to disclosing the minor's personal information to third parties.

bills.title: VCDPA Biometric Data Definition Expansion
bills.summary: Would expand the definition of biometric data to include data generated from photographs and recordings, as well as certain HIPAA-covered data and neural data.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework with Data Broker Registry
bills.summary: Del. Runion (R) introduced an App Store Accountability Act framework aligning with the models enacted in Utah, Louisiana, and Texas in 2025, with a private right of action. Del. Maldonado (D) introduced a separate data broker bill requiring data brokers to maintain a comprehensive information security program and establish a data broker registry with a $100,000 annual registration fee.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Del. Runion (R) and Del. Maldonado (D)

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Would establish an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework requiring age verification and parental consent, with requirements for existing accounts and pre-installed apps.
bills.status_detail: Has already passed the House and on track to pass the Senate

bills.title: Parents Over Platforms Act Age Signals Framework
bills.summary: Mirrors the Parents Over Platforms Act requiring application distribution providers to ask account holders to declare their age and provide developers the ability to call an age signal.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Way (R), proposes an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Introduced by the Senate Judiciary Committee, proposes an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by the Senate Judiciary Committee

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Calatayud (R), would establish an App Store Accountability Act framework similar to models enacted in Utah, Louisiana, and Texas in 2025, including specific requirements to age verify and provide consent options for existing accounts and preinstalled apps, and maintaining application exemptions.

bills.title: Interactive Computer Service Age Verification and Social Media Protections
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Hood (R), would create requirements for interactive computer services to implement age verification and obtain parental consent for minors to create and hold accounts, and provide parents access to minor's account activity. Would also require digital service providers to implement age verification and obtain parental consent for minors, restrict certain data processing activities, and implement strategies to prevent minor exposure to harmful content.

bills.title: Social Media Platform Product Liability Amendment
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. DeBoer, would amend the Parental Rights in Social Media Act enacted in 2025 to add language stating that a social media platform is considered a product for purposes of product liability actions provided under state law.

bills.title: Online Platform Minor Protections Budget Bill
bills.summary: Included in the budget bill, would cover operators of online platforms allowing users to create profiles, communicate, post content, create games, or exchange digital currency. Covered platforms would be obligated to conduct age assurance and, for minors, implement specific privacy defaults, disable integrated AI companions by default, and provide parents with tools for limiting transactions. Would also require additional parental consent for certain features for minors under 13.
bills.status_detail: Included in the New York state budget bill

bills.title: Social Media Age Verification and Minor Account Restrictions
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Jech (R), would require social media companies to freeze all user accounts upon effectiveness and conduct age verification on all platform users before allowing continued account use. If a user is determined to be a minor, platforms must implement privacy defaults, limit daily use to 1 hour per day, and provide parents with oversight tools.

bills.title: Interactive Computer Service Minor Account Protections
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Grellner (R), would require interactive computer services to implement age verification and obtain parental consent for minors to create and hold accounts, and prohibit certain activities such as communications between a minor and adult or access to harmful material without parental consent.

bills.title: Age-Appropriate Design Code (AADC)
bills.summary: An AADC-style framework. The legislature quickly passed this bill with amendments including adjustments to definitions, Nebraska AADC-style requirements for tools a covered online service must provide, and the bill's effective date being upon the Governor's approval. The bill is in the ratification process before moving on to Governor McMaster.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers with amendments; in ratification process before Governor McMaster

bills.title: NYCDPA Amendment for Enhanced Child Data Protections
bills.summary: A carryover bill introduced by Sen. Gounardes (D) that would add to the Child Data Protection Act passed in 2024, including more data management requirements aligned with comprehensive privacy laws and risk assessment requirements similar to AADCs.
bills.status_detail: Carryover bill; no significant movement yet

bills.title: VCDPA Verifiable Parental Consent Requirement for Minors
bills.summary: Would require a controller or processor to obtain verifiable parental consent prior to registering any child under 18 with the controller's product or service, or collecting, using, or disclosing the child's personal data. The parent or guardian must have the opportunity to consent to collection and use without consenting to disclosure to third parties.

bills.title: VCDPA Minor Access Rights and Advertising Requirements
bills.summary: Would amend the VCDPA to add a heightened access right for minors, prohibit controllers from entering into a user agreement with minors unless the controller obtains verifiable parental consent, and add new advertising disclosure requirements towards minors.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Goeben (R), proposes an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.

bills.title: Social Media Age Verification and Teen Privacy Protections
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Shimizu (R), would establish requirements related to minor online protections. Section one would require social media platforms to implement age verification and obtain parental consent for minors before providing addictive feeds. Section two would establish heightened privacy protections for teens ages 13-18, requiring platforms to obtain teen consent for processing, implement data minimization, and enable privacy defaults.

bills.title: Social Media Platform Prohibition on Minor Accounts
bills.summary: Introduced by Sen. Keohokalole (D), would prohibit social media platforms from allowing known minors to create or hold accounts. Would require platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent individuals under 16 from holding accounts, such as implementing age screens and terminating accounts of users once the platform knows the user is under 16.

bills.title: Social Media Age Verification and Parental Consent Requirements
bills.summary: Introduced by the House Committee on State Affairs, would require covered social media providers to implement age verification and obtain parental consent for minors under 16 to create accounts. Platforms would also be required to implement parental controls, restrict certain platform functions by default, and conduct ongoing age estimation checks on users for 7 years after account creation.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by the House Committee on State Affairs

bills.title: Social Media Age Verification and Parental Consent Requirements
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. King (R), would establish similar requirements as Idaho's H 542 but defines minor as anyone under 14 and includes additional requirements for establishing privacy defaults.

bills.title: Social Media Minor Account Restrictions and Addictive Design Prohibition
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Murray (D), would require social media platforms to conduct age verification, terminate accounts of users under 14, allow verified parents or guardians to request deletion of a minor's account, and disable addictive or manipulative design features targeting minors.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Governor Ivey signed this bill into law on February 17. The Act has an effective date of January 1, 2027. Largely aligns with Texas, Utah, and Louisiana ASAA laws from 2025 but with key differences including extending requirements to existing accounts, requiring parental consent for pre-installed apps, removing application exemptions, and adopting a definition for in-app purchases. Does not include a private right of action.
bills.status_detail: Signed into law by Governor Ivey on February 17, 2026. Effective January 1, 2027.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Introduced by Del. Nkongolo (R) on February 11, proposes an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Del. Nkongolo (R) on February 11, 2026

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Passed out of the Senate Judiciary committee on February 17 with amendments including adding a definition for in-app purchases limiting the term to purchases of digital currency or goods, clarifying the effective date as January 1, 2027, and removing the proposed private right of action.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of Senate Judiciary committee on February 17, 2026 with amendments

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Dietz (R) on February 12, would establish an App Store Accountability Act framework aligning with the models enacted in Utah, Louisiana, and Texas in 2025.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Rep. Dietz (R) on February 12, 2026

bills.title: Social Media Platform Minor Access Restrictions
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Marquez (D) on February 9, would require social media platforms to restrict minors under 16 from accessing the platform, develop and maintain reasonable safeguards mitigating foreseeable risks of harm, and publish a written safety and risk mitigation policy.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Rep. Marquez (D) on February 9, 2026

bills.title: Social Media Platform Prohibition on Minor Accounts
bills.summary: Would ban social media platforms from allowing minors under 16 to create or hold accounts. Was reported from the Senate Labor and Technology committee on February 6, then passed second reading before being referred to the Senate Consumer Protection committee for additional consideration on February 11.
bills.status_detail: Reported from Senate Labor and Technology committee on February 6, 2026; referred to Senate Consumer Protection committee on February 11, 2026

bills.title: Social Media Age Assurance and Minor Account Restrictions
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Tarver on February 4, would require social media platforms to implement an age assurance system and restrict children under 16 from creating or holding an account. Provides an exception where a child's parent allows use of an account held by the parent or guardian. Platforms may enter into agreements with application distributors and device manufacturers to share age data for compliance.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Rep. Tarver on February 4, 2026

bills.title: Online Safety Centers and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Introduced by Rep. Ventura on February 3, would require social media platforms to establish online safety centers and public cyberbullying policies. Would also prohibit controllers offering online services to known minors from engaging in dark patterns, offering direct messaging features to minors unless certain safeguards are in place, or using design features to significantly prolong a minor's use of the service.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Rep. Ventura on February 3, 2026

bills.title: Social Media Age Assurance and Parental Controls
bills.summary: Sponsored by Sen. Raatz (R), passed the House with amendments on February 17 and now returns to the Senate for consideration. Would require platforms to implement age assurance and obtain verifiable parental consent for minors under 17 to create and hold user accounts, establish parental controls and oversight mechanisms, prevent minor access to certain platform features, and conduct ongoing age checks on users after specified periods of platform use.
bills.status_detail: Passed the House with amendments on February 17, 2026; returned to Senate for consideration

bills.title: Social Media Age Verification and Parental Consent Requirements
bills.summary: Introduced by the Kansas House Committee on Legislative Modernization on February 3, would require social media platforms to implement age verification and obtain verifiable parental consent for minors under 16 to create or hold accounts. Platforms would also be required to allow parents to revoke consent and request account deletion at any time.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by the House Committee on Legislative Modernization on February 3, 2026

bills.title: Prohibition on Addictive Feeds for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit providing addictive feeds to minors and sending notifications during specific timeframes. Passed out of committee and was placed on second reading on February 10, 2026.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of committee and placed on second reading on February 10, 2026
